HMW-V21

"How might we give FM dispatchers a print-ready driver job sheet — without adding a separate print workflow to the vendor app?"
Root cause: When an FM job is assigned to a driver, the dispatcher needs to hand them physical or digital job details before departure: pickup address, delivery address, cargo counts, time window, and a reference number for WeChat coordination. Currently there is no way to get this from the Teleport OS vendor app. Dispatchers screenshot the screen, type manually into WeChat, or maintain a parallel Excel template. No standard format → errors, missing information, delays at pickup.

Context: FM trucking in Chinese cross-border logistics still relies heavily on paper job sheets (派车单) handed to drivers before departure. Even where drivers use WeChat, dispatchers send a structured text block ("DO ref, pickup address, delivery address, bags count, time"). The job sheet must work at 768px tablet (dispatcher's screen at warehouse), survive printing on basic A4 thermal printers common at logistics offices, and optionally be forwarded via WeChat.
Three options:
  1. Option A — Browser @media print: Add "Print" button to Job Detail header. A print CSS stylesheet hides all navigation and renders a clean A4 job sheet when the user triggers Ctrl+P or clicks Print.
  2. Option B — Copy-for-WeChat button: A "📋 Copy" button on the Job Detail page copies a structured plain-text block to clipboard. Dispatcher pastes directly into WeChat to the driver. No paper, no new screen.
  3. Option C — Print preview modal: "Print Job Sheet" button opens a full-screen modal with the exact A4 layout rendered on screen. Dispatcher reviews before sending to printer. Modal has [Print] and [Copy for WeChat] actions.

Option A — Browser print via @media print CSS

Option A

A dedicated "Print Job Sheet" button is added to the Job Detail page header action area (next to "← My Jobs"). Clicking it triggers window.print(). A @media print stylesheet hides the nav, status bar, and action buttons, and renders the job details in a clean A4 job-sheet format. The vendor app's existing layout reflows into the print layout — no extra screens required.

Pros
  • Zero new UI screen or modal — print CSS only
  • Works offline; no network needed to print
  • Standard browser workflow dispatchers already know
  • One-time CSS addition covers all FM jobs forever
Cons
  • Print preview dialog varies across browsers and printers
  • Dispatcher cannot preview what will print before triggering dialog
  • No digital share option — driver still needs a physical copy or WhatsApp
  • Relies on CSS @media print — harder to maintain as page evolves

Option B — Copy for WeChat (clipboard text)

Option B

A "📋 Copy" button copies a structured text block in Chinese logistics format to the clipboard. Dispatcher pastes directly into a WeChat message to the driver. No print required. This matches existing real-world behavior in Chinese 3PL dispatch — coordinators already exchange job info via WeChat text; the goal is standardizing the format, not changing the channel.

Copies formatted text block to clipboard
Clipboard preview (what gets pasted into WeChat):
【Teleport OS 派车单】 单号: DO-008 / J04 客户: TikTok 服务: FM Trucking (FM) MAWB: 172-1234 5678 📍 提货 深圳平湖物流中心 2026年4月26日 09:30 📍 送货 香港机场货站 Cathay Cargo Village 2026年4月26日 15:00 📦 货物: 24件 / 1,280 kg 🚚 车牌: 粤B·12345 (5T) Teleport OS 联系: ops@teleport.it
After clicking Copy for WeChat: A green toast "Copied to clipboard" appears for 2 seconds. Dispatcher opens WeChat on their tablet → long-press in chat → Paste → Send. The text block includes Chinese field labels (提货/送货/货物) because drivers communicate in Chinese even within international logistics companies.
Pros
  • Works on tablets without printers at site
  • Aligns with real-world WeChat logistics coordination
  • Instant — no dialog, no paper, no printer required
  • Chinese labels appropriate for driver-facing content
  • Zero layout risk — pure JavaScript clipboard API
Cons
  • Text-only: no QR code, no map link, no structured data
  • Formatting collapses in some WeChat versions
  • No paper copy for gate checks at cargo terminals
  • No audit trail — system can't confirm driver received info

Option C — Print-preview modal (recommended)

Option C — Recommended

A "Print Job Sheet" button opens a full-screen modal that renders the exact A4 job sheet layout on screen before printing. Dispatcher reviews the sheet, then clicks [Print A4] (triggers window.print()) or [Copy for WeChat] (clipboard text from Option B). This gives the dispatcher confidence in what gets printed, without the surprise of browser print preview formatting differences.

Pros
  • What-you-see-is-what-prints — no surprise from browser print dialog
  • Both print and copy-for-WeChat in one surface
  • Modal pattern is already in the design system (slide-out precedent)
  • A4 sheet can be styled for thermal printers used at logistics sites

  • Print from modal via window.print() still triggers browser print dialog (one unavoidable step)

✓ Recommendation: Option C (print preview modal) + Option B (copy for WeChat)

Implement Option C: a "Print Job Sheet" button in the FM job detail header opens a modal with the exact A4 layout. The modal also contains "Copy for WeChat" (Option B) so dispatchers who don't have a printer can still standardize their WeChat job handover format.

Trigger: Button only appears on FM jobs with a driver assigned. On non-FM jobs or jobs without a driver, the button is absent (no driver to hand a sheet to).

Print CSS: The A4 print layout should be a dedicated hidden <div id="print-only"> injected into the DOM when the modal is open, targeted by @media print { body > * { display: none } #print-only { display: block } }. This is more reliable than transforming the existing page via CSS.

QR code: In v1, render a static placeholder QR square (gray box). In v1.1 when the WeChat mini program exists, generate a real QR linking to weixin://dl/jobdetail?j=J04&token=abc using a QR library. The field slot is already reserved in the layout.

Open questions:

  • Should the WeChat text use Chinese or English labels, or bilingual? Recommend: Chinese primary labels (提货/送货), English reference numbers and location names (dispatchers are bilingual; drivers read Chinese).
  • Should the job sheet include vendor emergency contact? Useful if driver can't reach dispatcher. Recommend: yes — pull from vendor profile (v1.1 when vendor profile is built).
  • Should print history be logged in the activity log ("Job sheet printed — 26 Apr 09:14")? Recommend: yes, as an audit trace for dispatcher accountability.
